interface.title: iNatGaps — Sampling Gap Explorer
interface.field: Biodiversity informatics / citizen-science ecology (field survey planning)
interface.stage_of_work: Planning: choosing where to collect new field observations
interface.what_it_is_for: Lay a grid over a place or a drawn area, count iNaturalist records in each cell for a chosen taxon and date range, rank the cells by how under-sampled they are, inspect any cell's species and observers, and export the ranked grid for field planning.

data.note: No bundled data. Everything was fetched live from public services during the session: iNaturalist place search, counts, grid tiles and species lists; OpenStreetMap place outlines; Esri basemaps. Regions used: Ventura County, CA (iNat place), a hand-drawn rectangle over the San Fernando Valley, and Topanga State Park (OSM outline). The Public lands (beta) overlay failed with a 'No public-lands service responded' error. Per-cell scan progress usually moved only while the browser was being used, which may be headless timer throttling.

tree.general: Find the least-sampled parts of a study area and plan where to collect new observations
tree.specific: Rank grid cells of a region by how few iNaturalist records they have (survey priority), inspect candidate cells, and export the ranked grid as CSV/GeoJSON

features.name: Tile-based bulk counter
features.general: Count many small cells at once by reading whole pre-aggregated map tiles, so a large area at fine resolution needs only a handful of requests
features.specific: Fast mode (beta) swaps Grid cell for 'Tile zoom → cell size' and counts each map tile in one request (Ventura County: 1,503 cells from 7 tile requests); tiles are cached for the session
steps: check Fast mode (beta)
pick a tile zoom, which sets the cell size
run the scan; each tile request fills all the cells inside it
re-run from the session tile cache
serves_tasks: Run a fast whole-tile count for a large area at fine resolution

features.name: Skip-empty-areas block counting
features.general: Cut the number of remote queries by counting large blocks first and only asking about individual cells inside blocks that have records
features.specific: Skip empty areas checkbox (on by default) in standard mode. In the replay, 40 cells were counted with 8 requests sent and 27 from saved counts. The run itself only saw this path stall at 0/44 on Ventura County. The coarse-block-first method is described by the README; the runs saw only the request totals
steps: leave Skip empty areas checked (or uncheck it to query every cell)
press Analyze live region
read requests sent vs cells counted in the status line
serves_tasks: Run an exact count query over the grid
